newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Hilton, PaineWebber hit actives.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Hilton, PaineWebber hit actives.

text.p: Big trades were seen in selected options on shares of Hilton Hotels Corp and PaineWebber Group Inc on Monday.
Traders said the action in the Hilton November 26-1/4 and 27-1/2 calls and the January 28-3/4 calls was likely an investor rolling out a position.
They said the PaineWebber volume -- 11,270 contracts of the January 25 call -- was probably an investor protecting a stock position.
Hilton shares ended up 1/2 at 29-1/2 and PaineWebber finished unchanged at 24-1/4.

"A lot of people who have large positions left over from the October expiration -- with this merger/acquisition in the final stages -- are just rolling their options," said a trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange.
Hilton acquired Bally Entertainment Corp in a $3.0 billion deal that is expected to close by the end of the year.
The Hilton November 26-1/4 call traded about 7,800 contracts, the November 27-1/2 call traded 1,290 and the January 28-3/4 call traded about 9,130.
Traders said the activity appeared to be related.
The trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange added that, while the volume was high, it was not a dramatic change from the heavy trading seen in the options over the past month or so.
Michael Schwartz at Oppenheimer & Co, said some of the January volume could have been done to hedge the November positions.
On the Chicago Board Options Exchange, traders said the heavy volume in the PaineWebber January 25 call was mainly from one block of 8,700 contracts.
"The stock's had quite a rally, so it could be just somebody putting on a buy-write," said one trader.
He explained the investor could have bought the shares at a lower price and was selling the calls to protect the stock position.
PaineWebber shares were trading around 20-1/2 a month ago.
